name: Even Number Addicts
description: Alice and Bob are playing a game on a sequence $$$a_1, a_2, \dots, a_n$$$ of length $$$n$$$. They move in turns and Alice moves first . In the turn of each player, he or she should select an integer and remove it from the sequence. The game ends when there is no integer left in the sequence. Alice wins if the sum of her selected integers is even ; otherwise, Bob wins. Your task is to determine who will win the game, if both players play optimally.
input_specification: Each test contains multiple test cases. The first line contains an integer $$$t$$$ ($$$1 \leq t \leq 100$$$) — the number of test cases. The following lines contain the description of each test case. The first line of each test case contains an integer $$$n$$$ ($$$1 \leq n \leq 100$$$), indicating the length of the sequence. The second line of each test case contains $$$n$$$ integers $$$a_1, a_2, \dots, a_n$$$ ($$$-10^9 \leq a_i \leq 10^9$$$), indicating the elements of the sequence.
output_specification: For each test case, output " Alice " (without quotes) if Alice wins and " Bob " (without quotes) otherwise.
approach_summary: Apply Knapsack and Basic Dynamic Programming paradigm under the Dynamic Programming (DP) framework. Exploit problem invariants to reduce state space and achieve optimal complexity.
